en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew says only 'a holy thing to the LORD'.

01.r: Every part of the land's tithe, without exception.
01.n: The word is a noun, 'the whole', joined to what follows; BDB notes that English often renders it 'all' or 'every' to avoid stiffness. The BSB's 'Thus' renders the 'and'.

02.r: The tenth part of the produce, owed to God.
02.n: Gesenius gives the meaning 'tithes', from the noun for 'ten'. Our register renders this word 'tithe' throughout.

03.r: The farmland and what it yields.
03.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as THE EARTH; BDB: earth, land. Here it is the land as a source of crops.

04.r: The grain crop raised from seed.
04.n: Gesenius: seed, that which is scattered, whether of plants, trees or grain. The 'from' marks a part taken out of the whole. The DRC says simply 'of corn', that is, grain.

06.n: Gesenius: fruit, whether of the earth and field or of a tree. The Hebrew lists seed and fruit with no 'or' between them; the translations add 'or' or 'and'.

07.n: Singular, but Gesenius notes the word is often collective, 'trees'.

08.r: The tithe is the LORD's property.
08.n: Literally 'to the LORD': the 'to' marks the owner.

09.r: Picks up the long subject: all of it.
09.n: The pronoun 'it' gathers up the long list before it. In the Hebrew it stands after 'to the LORD', 'to the LORD it (is)', so we render 'it is the LORD's'; the next clause has no pronoun of its own.

10.r: Set apart for God, not for common use.
10.n: A noun, 'holiness' or 'a holy thing', not an adjective; Gesenius gives first 'holiness', and the brief's lexicon 'apartness, sacredness'. The translations render it as a description, 'holy' or 'sanctified'.

11.r: Holy as belonging to the LORD.

_extra.9: καὶ (and): the Greek joins seed and fruit with 'and'; the Hebrew lists them without one.

01.n: The Greek has no 'and': 'every tenth of the land'.

02.n: δεκάτη, a tenth, the word our register renders 'tenth' in the New Testament.

04.n: σπέρμα, seed: the source of English 'sperm'.

07.n: ξύλινος is an adjective, 'of wood', used here for trees: 'the fruit of the woody (plant)'.

09.n: ἐστίν, 'is': the Greek has a verb where the Hebrew has a pronoun.

10.n: ἅγιον, an adjective, 'holy', where the Hebrew has the noun 'a holy thing'.
